summary: Compares include_* vs import_*: dynamic vs static, runtime vs parse-time, task options applying to the include only vs all child tasks, looping support, visibility in --list-tags/--list-tasks, handler notification, and --start-at-task. Recommends one approach per playbook.
questions: Can I use --start-at-task with included tasks?
Why don't tags inside includes show up in --list-tags?
Can I use import_tasks in a loop?
Should I mix includes and imports in one playbook?

answer_card.title: include_* vs import_* compared
answer_card.answer_md:
| | include_* | import_* |
|---|---|---|
| Reuse | Dynamic | Static |
| Processed | At runtime | At parse time |
| Task options | Include task only | All child tasks |
| Loops | Once per item | Not allowed |
| `--list-tags` / `--list-tasks` | Inner items not listed | All listed |
| Handlers | Can't notify tasks inside | Can notify imported handlers |
| `--start-at-task` | Can't start inside | Can |

Pick one approach per playbook; mixing can cause hard-to-diagnose bugs.
